title: Closing a Commercial Credit Account
content:
A customer-requested closure of a Commercial Credit Account is accepted only when the account's receivable balance is zero and no dispute on the account is open; a customer with a credit balance first receives the refund under the refund and small-balance write-off rules, and a customer with a debit balance first pays it.

### Clauses

1. The closure is the customer's own act and is confirmed by the customer; the account stays active until then.
2. An active account with a zero balance and no posted invoice for the tier's dormancy period in whole months is closed by the system as dormant.
3. An account in collections whose referred balance Corbett Collections writes off is closed as a collections write-off and cannot be reopened; the customer must apply again.
4. Closing the credit account ends terms billing for every program and ship-to of the customer; any program that bills monthly must be on a different payment arrangement before closure, which is outside this charter.

### Dormancy period by tier

The dormancy period of every tier is that tier's own dormancy figure in whole months:

| Tier | Dormancy period |
|---|---|
| Corbett Net 10 Starter Account | the tier's dormancy figure (18 months) |
| Corbett Net 30 Standard Account | the tier's dormancy figure (24 months) |
| Corbett Net 30 Preferred Account | the tier's dormancy figure (24 months) |
| Corbett Net 45 Business Account | the tier's dormancy figure (24 months) |
| Corbett Net 60 Corporate Account | the tier's dormancy figure (36 months) |
| Corbett Net 90 Strategic Account | the tier's dormancy figure (36 months) |

### Closure check

| Receivable balance | Open dispute | Customer-requested closure |
|---|---|---|
| zero | none | accepted |
| zero | one open | not accepted |
| credit balance | — | not accepted until the balance is refunded |
| debit balance | — | not accepted until the balance is paid |
